title: Kainen's theorem on chromatic number and edge cuts
statement: Let $G$ be a finite graph, let $X$ be a set of its vertices with complement $V \setminus X$, and let $n$ be a natural number. Suppose that the subgraphs induced on $X$ and on $V \setminus X$ are each $n$-colourable, and that the edge cut between the two parts contains fewer than $n$ edges — that is, the number of edges having one endpoint in $X$ and the other in $V \setminus X$ is at most $n-1$. Then $G$ is itself $n$-colourable.
